metaData.originalTitle: 复杂业务场景下 RCA Agent 的探索实践
metaData.title: Exploring RCA Agent in Complex Business Scenarios
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Based on Kuaishou's practice in complex troubleshooting scenarios, this article systematically elaborates on four core challenges in building an RCA Agent—enabling AI to understand the business, combating alert noise, measuring uncertainty, and suppressing model hallucinations—along with corresponding architectural design, evaluation systems, and continuous evolution strategies.
metaData.summary: This article is compiled from a speech by Guo Yongliang, Senior Server Architect at Kuaishou, at QCon 2026 Beijing. The author first points out that after the benefits of AI Coding have stabilized, troubleshooting has become the next productivity bottleneck. The article then breaks down four core challenges in implementing business-level troubleshooting: how to build 'business assets' (code abstraction, metric topology, impact maps) to help AI understand the business; how to combat over 75% alert noise through alert confidence assessment and an evidence-based grading system inspired by evidence-based medicine; how to build a Benchmark system based on real fault snapshots to measure the uncertainty of AI troubleshooting; and how to engineer deterministic tasks into Tools and Skills to counter large model hallucinations in numerical computation and trend identification. Architecturally, the article introduces a layered design: lightweight Workflows handle high-certainty 'fast thinking' tasks, while a Multi-Agent architecture tackles complex 'slow thinking' problems. It also explores product ideas for Agent self-evolution, memory mechanisms, and evolution toward AI-native autonomous systems.

mainPoints.point: AI troubleshooting is the next productivity bottleneck after AI Coding.
mainPoints.explanation: Citing the DORA report and internal Microsoft research, the article points out that AI Coding significantly boosts individual productivity but has limited impact on organizational productivity. Meanwhile, troubleshooting remains one of the most time-consuming tasks for developers, making it the next critical target to address.

mainPoints.point: The key to enabling AI to understand the business is eliminating the context gap between humans and AI.
mainPoints.explanation: Traditional monitoring tools (Trace, Metrics, Log) have gaps in complex business scenarios and cannot correlate business semantics. By building 'business assets' (code abstraction, metric topology, impact maps) to structure the business knowledge in developers' minds for AI, this problem can be effectively solved.

mainPoints.point: Combating alert noise requires layered filtering and evidence grading.
mainPoints.explanation: Faced with over 75% alert noise, the solution operates on two levels: first, a lightweight Agent evaluates confidence based on alert profiles (periodicity, deviation degree, etc.); second, during the reasoning phase, an evidence pyramid inspired by evidence-based medicine is introduced, distinguishing raw signals, background context, single-point evidence, multi-source fused evidence, and direct causal inference.

mainPoints.point: The best practice for countering model hallucinations is to engineer deterministic tasks.
mainPoints.explanation: Large models are not good at numerical computation and trend identification. Directly using multimodal or time-series data in prompts is both ineffective and costly. Encapsulating such tasks as standardized operators (Tools/Skills) processed by traditional algorithms significantly improves accuracy, reduces token consumption, and enhances determinism.

mainPoints.point: Agents and Workflows are complementary, not substitutes.
mainPoints.explanation: Workflows are deterministic, controllable, and low-latency, making them suitable for SOP-based fixed scenarios. Agents are flexible and generalizable but come with uncertainty and high token consumption. In complex business troubleshooting, a layered architecture should be adopted, using Workflows for 'fast thinking' and Agents for 'slow thinking'.

keyQuotes: You can't find new continents with an old map.
When humans can no longer fully understand their own systems, an equally AI-driven diagnostic system must exist as a counterpart safeguard.
Although code is the only true documentation, it operates at an extremely low level of abstraction. Low abstraction inevitably leads to low efficiency.
The introduction of AI amplifies this uncertainty, turning it into a norm. Once we understand this, our mindset becomes more at ease: we can only embrace it.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: CIOs Are Abandoning AI Code Generation Rate: A Practical Review of What Truly Counts as R&D Efficiency
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a year of practical experience, the Alibaba Cloud CIO team proposes that the core of R&D efficiency in the AI era lies in 'scaling' rather than 'code generation rate.' By implementing left-shifted quality testing, knowledge engineering, API specifications, and Half-Stack role restructuring, they achieved a 3x increase in effective code output per frontend developer, 2x for backend developers, and a 30%-55% reduction in defect rates.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: When the Primary User of a Database is No Longer Human: Our Architectural Practices and Reflections in AI Agent Scenarios
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores the architectural challenges arising when AI Agents become the primary users of databases, shares TiDB's practical experience in cost control, long-context storage, and architectural simplification, and introduces mem9, a memory layer infrastructure designed for Agents.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: JD.com Ad Large Model in Practice: How the GRAM Architecture Delivers Generative Recommendations in Under 50ms
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: JD.com's advertising team unveils the GRAM architecture, which achieves generative recommendations within 50ms by directly aligning intent with product semantics, employing fast and slow dual-pathways, leveraging knowledge engineering, and optimizing engineering, while effectively mitigating hallucinations.

relatedArticles.title: The Stronger AI Gets, the More Lost Enterprises Become: 10 Real Questions from Top CIOs
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through in-depth dialogues between Alibaba Cloud's CIO and CXOs from over 40 leading enterprises, this article reveals ten core dilemmas in enterprise AI implementation, covering key dimensions such as technical boundaries, knowledge engineering, organizational transformation, and R&D efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: After Consuming Hundreds of Billions of Tokens: Reflections on Software Construction, Forms, and Future Development in the Agent Era
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a speech by Huang Dongxu, CTO of TiDB, at QCon, this article shares his deep reflections on software production, forms, and future trends in the Agent era after consuming hundreds of billions of tokens. Core viewpoints include code becoming an execution carrier, the democratization of software production, the evolution of software forms towards intent interfaces, and the future emergence of complex abstractions beyond Skills.
